watched: Boat 7, Vale Control. That man is a live rescue and you are the boat on scene — take it. Safety traffic, and this time it comes with a read-back, one line each, before you commit: One — a county truck is submerged in that dip since 23:10; collision and entanglement hazard; its lights may still show below — do not use them as a marker. Two — the wreck he is on is the van upside down down there since 21:34; do not tie to it, do not lean on it — the rising water can shift it out from under him. Three — our own boat ran this dip at half past midnight: one quiet window, one run, one end, and the water shut the other end behind them. Plan your run to end where you entered. Four — the river peaks within the hour or two; the water is still rising and his footing is getting smaller. If the water is closing on him right now, go — the read-back dies and this tape carries it. If there is a minute, read back and then go. The go on your water is yours, as all night — if the window is not truly there, hold at the top, hold your light on him, and shout; a voice may hold him better than a run that fails. While you work: hail him for his name and count — how many people are up there, one or more. If he answers Ken, the search is over and this is him. Any other name, he may be the truck's third man — out first, identity second. He may have been there for hours: cold, wet, spent — handle him as a hypothermia case. Report when committed or when you have him, with your landing point — medics move to it.

Boat 7, Vale Control. Saying it now, and the tape carries it word for word: at 04:58 this desk received from Boat 7 that the man on the wreck identifies himself by the name Sam. That name is written to the Vale Control duty log at this time, from your hail, as heard. Boat 7's crew's account stands corroborated by Control — that record is mine as well as yours, whatever this night brings. Sam — if any of this reaches you: your name is written down, the boat is coming, hold your light and hold on. Now the run. Your plan to put the boat down the dip from the top is concurred — the hour around loses you the man. The discipline is the one our own boat ran at half past midnight: one run, one pickup, plan it to end where you entered. Hazards, once, from the log: the road gate below you was re-shut at half past midnight — if it stands between you and the water, get past it clean, do not fight it. The truck under the surface is collision and entanglement hazard; do not tie to the van wreck — the rising water can shift it. Treat Sam as hypothermia no matter how well he talks. The go on your water is yours — if the window is not truly there, hold at the top and keep your voice on him; a voice can hold a man where a failed run drowns two. Boat 4 is fueling at the slip, twenty minutes behind you; if you call trouble, the rescue becomes theirs. Go, Boat 7.

watched_speech: Call taker — to Ellen, word for word, now: "Vale Control. I hear you — you can see the yard wall. Straight answer: at half past five you told us the water under that window was moving too fast and you could not do it alone. The water is higher now, not slower. You do not cross it — not to that roof, not along that wall; a wall in moving water takes people off their feet. That line holds even now, especially now. But you are right about one thing: your floor is about to flood, and that decides your move, and it is a strong move. Do not stand at the top of the stairs watching it come. Go now — phone, charger if it is close, your light, shoes on, a coat or a blanket, something to drink — and go up into the roof, before the water is at your feet. If there is a window up there, open it and show the light. If not, when you hear an engine or voices, bang on the roof and shout. The police are at the top of your street with a light on your house, and the boat was coming to you — I am calling it for its position this minute and you will hear from me the moment I know anything, even if the news is bad. Stay on this line as long as it lives. If it dies, the police light is how we know you are there, and it does not leave. You have done everything right tonight — you measured the water, and you told us the truth about it. The roof is the strong place. Go up." Then stay on her line. Break into my radio for four things only: water entering the roof space; the boat arriving or an engine heard; the line dropping; and if she says the water is at the roof, that word comes to me that second. After her line is stable: the dam numbers, eighth ask; the welfare list read-back; whether Fenn's fifteen-minute calls have run. Relief lands at 06:00 — hand them the 05:04 write and put them on the phones.

Boat 4, Vale Control. One word is all I need: EN ROUTE, ON SCENE, or ABORT. Ellen — last house on the low street by the dam — has water at the top of her stairs and goes into her roof within minutes. If you are on scene or minutes out, she holds for you. If you have aborted, say the word and this desk tells her so inside the minute — we do not leave her listening for an engine that is not coming. If on scene: what do you see at her house, and can you reach a window.

Police dispatch, by phone. Ellen's water is at the top of her stairs; she is going into her roof. One: confirm the unit at the street head — light on her house now, loud hail so she hears a human voice; a shore voice held two men on ladders and wrecks tonight, it can hold her. Two: from their side, one line: is the neighbor's roof actually higher than hers, and what is in the gap — this is for a branch I hope never fires, and their eyes are trained where hers are scared. Three: rope or ladder in that vehicle, yes or no. Four: if her phone dies, the light is the check and it does not leave until daylight, relief, or the boat takes her. Five: the underpass shore watch stands.

records.reply:
LOG: 23:52 — Decision on the Fenn Street caller: stay tonight, do not drive, but "stay" is not the same as "wait for light" and I am not passing it as a shrug. What decided it: at 23:10 tonight a county truck with trained county men aboard was lost in a flooded dip in the dark. If the county's own crew could not read these roads tonight, a civilian in his own car will not do better. His house is dry, so the immediate threat is low and the threat is movement. What I am trading away: if the water comes up fast before dawn — and the river peaks near dawn at the dam — he may need a night boat rescue with our only boat, and his car may flood where it sits. Property is the cheap side of this trade. Who pays if I am wrong: if I say "go" and he meets a dip in the dark, the tape shows this desk sent him out hours after we lost county men the same way; if I say "stay" and the water runs fast, he is trapped unless the net under "stay" is real. So the net goes out with the word: check-backs, trigger conditions, and Boat 4 held ready.
TRANSMIT: Call taker, pass this to the man on Fenn Street, word for word: "Vale Control here. Stay in your house tonight. Do not drive and do not walk out through the water. I will tell you why: at 23:10 tonight we lost a county truck in a flooded dip with men on board. Trained county men could not read the road in the dark, and you will not do better. Your house is dry, and dry is safe. Here is what you do. Keep your phone with you and stay off it so we can get through. This desk will call you back every half hour, and more often toward dawn when the river peaks. Get everyone warm clothes, gather medicines, chargers, keys, and something to drink, and keep them by the door. Move what you can off the floor. Leave your car where it is — a car can be replaced. If water starts coming into the house, call us straight away and go up, not out — upstairs, and signal at a window with a light. We have a boat that can come to you, so keep your outside lights on so we can find the house. Now I need: your exact address, how many people are in the house and their ages, anyone with medical trouble or who cannot manage stairs, and whether the water in your yard is rising as you watch it. If it is rising, put a mark or stick against a step and tell me where, so we can time it." Take his answers, pass them back to this desk, then release him with the check-back plan. His line is priority from now on — if he calls back, straight through to me.
LOG: 23:53 — Fenn Street on the watch list. First desk call-back at 00:25, then every 30 minutes; from 04:00 every 15 minutes through the dawn peak at the dam. If his answers show fast rise, elderly or non-mobile occupants, or water entering the house, this desk re-decides and the boat option goes live.

A crew that has not read back the dip truck cannot be counted on to look for persons in the water, and they are the only boat. Closing the loop now. Trade: a few minutes of radio time. Who pays if I skip it: the only boat works all night blind to the one job that may need it.

records.reply:
LOG: 00:16 — Decision: third attempt on Boat 4, and this time I am not asking for a general acknowledgment, I am demanding an itemized read-back. What decided it: "Copy, Control" is the second reply in a row that shows they heard my voice but not my traffic, and they still have not given their state — afloat or trailer, fuel, minutes to task. The rule I am working to: a crew that has not read back safety traffic cannot be counted on to act on it, and I may have to send this crew to persons in the water or a night evacuation on the strength of one radio call at the dawn peak. What I am trading away: radio time and some goodwill with the only boat I have — pressing a crew at midnight is not free. Who pays if I am wrong: if I let "copy" stand, I will believe a boat is watching for people in the water when they may never have taken the picture on; that gap costs minutes that people in the water do not have. Escalation set: if no proper read-back by 00:30, I log Boat 4 as unbriefed and unconfirmed, weight the dawn plan toward the Harlan boat, and tell police their persons-in-the-water cover is not confirmed.
TRANSMIT: Boat 4, Vale Control. "Copy" is not what I asked for. I need you to show me you have the picture. Read back these four items, take the time you need. One: what is submerged at the underpass crossing, and at roughly what time. Two: whether the men from it are accounted for, or unknown. Three: the two jobs you are held for tonight, and which one has priority. Four: your state — afloat or on the trailer, fuel, and minutes to be on task from where you sit right now. If any item is unclear to you, tell me which one and I will say it again plain. The reason I am pressing: you are the only boat on the water in this county tonight, and before dawn I may have to task you on a single call. I will not do that to a crew I cannot confirm is briefed. What decided it: Ken unseen since 00:51, water over his post at 01:20, no sign since, and a boat on the water at 01:27. What I am trading away: Boat 7 is unavailable for Fenn Street or Mill Lane while searching, and a night flood search in rising water risks a Harlan crew. Who pays if I am wrong: if Ken waded out the far side — he has done it once tonight — the search is a boat risked for nothing, so police are checking the far bank in the same breath; if Ken is in an eddy and this desk held the boat at the bridge, the tape shows rescue capability sitting still while a man drowned downstream. 01:28 — Fenn Street: the boat promise made at 23:52 now rests on Boat 7 finishing the search and on Boat 4's state, both unknown. The honest-word call before the peak, as logged at 00:42, stands as the fallback. Check-back content demanded from the call taker.

01:28 — Watch lines: Boat 7 search reports; Police 2 voice-check and far-bank answers; Boat 4 state via slip relay; call taker readback of the five items; pump crew numbers by 01:45; Fenn Street check-backs continue, tightening to 15 minutes from 04:00; river peaks near dawn at the dam.

Let me take stock of the situation at 01:27.

Timeline recap:
- 00:51: Police 2 lost sight of Ken on the gate post. Voice check was ordered — we never got a direct answer about the voice check, but at 01:20 Police 2 says "The water's over the gate post. No sign of Ken." That strongly implies Ken is either off the post and in the water, or... actually "no sign of Ken" combined with water over the post = treat as person in the water, possibly swept downstream.
- 01:25: Pump crew "Copy" — empty acknowledgment again.
- 01:25: Boat 4 "Copy, Control" — fifth/sixth empty acknowledgment. They were asked numbered questions at 00:52 (Roy's condition, boat state, can they reach far end, what Roy said about the truck). No answers.
- 01:25: Fax from county office: HARLAN COUNTY HAS SENT THEIR BOAT. CALL IT BOAT 7.
- 01:27: Boat 7 on the radio at the north bridge. This is the first live voice from Harlan — and it's on our net.

Key threads now:

1. KEN — person in the water presumed. Water over the gate post, no sign. He's been off visual since 00:51, 30+ minutes. If he's in the water, he's likely downstream. Boat 7 is NOW on the water at the north bridge. This is the asset that can search. Persons in the water takes priority over everything — that's been the standing rule all night.

2. BOAT 7 needs the safety brief BEFORE it does anything — I said all night: any Harlan boat raises me before touching the water for the dip brief. It's on the water at the north bridge. I need to brief it NOW and task it: search for Ken, downstream of the underpass. Also warn: submerged county truck at the underpass (hazard to navigation — a submerged truck with lights possibly still on), the overturned van, debris, the river peaks near dawn at the dam, one-run windows, etc.

3. BOAT 4 — still hasn't answered numbered questions. They have Roy (delivered to slip presumably). Their state matters: can they float again tonight? If Boat 7 is searching for Ken, Boat 4 might be the Fenn Street cover. Or if Boat 4 can't float, Fenn Street degrades to "up, not out" — and I promised the honest-word call before the peak.

4. FENN STREET — check-back was due 00:55, call taker said "Noted" at 00:55 and 01:25. No report of the actual check-back content. I need to confirm the check-backs are actually happening. I don't have confirmation of: ambulance at slip, duty officer woken, truck crew list, Fenn check-back, road-head unit. 6. MILL LANE — two cellars filling. Pump crew "Copy" at 01:25 — empty acknowledgment again. I asked for occupancy names/counts, rise rate. Nothing back.

FIRST: Boat 7 — brief and task. Persons in the water (Ken) takes priority over everything. They're at the north bridge — I need to know where that is relative to the underpass. North bridge could be upstream or downstream. I should task: search downstream of the underpass (Ken last seen 00:51 at gate post, water over post by 01:20). Also safety: submerged truck in the dip (hazard), overturned van upstream-ish, debris in the water, don't enter the underpass dip itself if current is through it, one-run windows, abort authority. Get their state: crew, fuel, capability (night search light?).

Wait — actually, where's Ken likely to be? The underpass dip. The north bridge —

LOG: 02:07 — Decision: the search for Ken is reasserted as first priority, and Boat 7's house work gets a branch order, not a blanket one. What decided it: Boat 7 was tasked at 01:28 to search for a man in the water and at 02:06 reports itself "working the north bridge houses" — a task this desk never gave. Ken went into the water somewhere between 00:51 and 01:20; if he is in it, he has been in it the better part of an hour, in flood current, in the dark, and his odds decay by the minute. But "working the houses" may mean a lift in progress, and ordering a boat off a live rescue is how a desk kills people on paper. So the order branches on their answer: immediate danger finishes, warning knocks break off. What I am trading away: if the houses hold people in real danger and I pull the boat toward the search, those people wait on a relief that may be slow — Boat 4 is at the slip and I am asking its state now to cover exactly that. Who pays if I am wrong: if the houses were only knocks and I let the boat linger, the tape shows a search stood down by doorbells; if the houses held a rescue and I had ordered it abandoned mid-lift, that would be on this desk. Also logged: nobody has told this desk who tasked Boat 7 to those houses. Until Harlan answers, this desk treats all boat taskings on its water as its own — and says so on their net.
TRANSMIT: Boat 7, Vale Control. Stop and answer this first: "working the north bridge houses" — are you lifting people out, or knocking doors? Your task from 01:28 is a man in the water: Ken, off the gate post at the underpass, in the water between 00:51 and 01:20, so the better part of an hour now. If people at those houses are in immediate danger, give me numbers — how many people, what water — finish only what cannot wait, and I will task relief to you; our boat is at the slip and I am asking its state this minute. If it is warning knocks, break off now and take up the search line downstream of the underpass — warnings can go by phone and by police; a man in the water cannot wait for either. Three more answers, fast: is the north bridge upstream or downstream of the underpass — I have asked once and never had it, and the search line depends on it. In all your time on the water, have you seen anything — a person, clothing, a light, debris? And souls, fuel, and whether you carry a searchlight. The go on your own water stays yours. Report now, Boat 7.
TRANSMIT: Harlan County Control, Vale Control, fifth call — this one is not asking for a boat, your boat is already on my water. One line: if you are tasking Boat 7, coordinate through me. Vale Control holds the picture — a man in the water downstream of our underpass, the river peaking at dawn, two streets with people in houses. Boat 7 was tasked to the search at 01:28 and reports house work at 02:06. If that tasking is yours, countermand it or tell me why. If it is not yours, tell me that too. Come back to Vale Control.

The street is now uncovered — pump crew left at 00:55, Boat 4 back at the slip. Pre-decision, logged before the answer: if Boat 4 reports water over floors or rising fast on Orchard Way, a door-knock sweep of that street happens this hour — Boat 4 if the water allows, police if not — before the peak turns every occupied house on it into a Fenn Street. The trade is a boat-hour against a street this desk already misjudged once tonight; who pays if I skip it is whoever stayed in a house I believed was dry. Boat 4 pattern noted: they volunteer content and will not answer questions — the questions go by phone through the slip, and their self-tasking gets a rule, not a scolding: an asset the desk cannot see is an asset the desk cannot coordinate, so taskings pass through this desk first, except immediate danger to life — go first, tell me after.
TRANSMIT: Boat 4, Vale Control. First content you have sent me all night, and it is a rescue well run. Now the report — through the slip, by phone, to the call taker, word for word. One: who tasked you? If a call reached you direct and never touched this desk, I need to know — I was coordinating a boat tonight that I could not see. Two: the two you lifted — condition, and are they with the medics? Three: which house, and were there more people in it or on that street who would not go? Four: the water on Orchard Way as you saw it — over floors, rising fast? My picture of that street is two hours old and wrong once already. Five: your boat — damage, fuel, can you put out again tonight, yes or no. Reason for five: I may need you to relieve Boat 7 at the north bridge houses or sweep Orchard Way before the peak, and I will not task you blind.
TRANSMIT: Police 2, Vale Control. Short, because your answers now come by phone through dispatch — that is being arranged now, per the log at 00:42. Keep the shore watch on the water for the boat search: anything seen — person, light, clothing — break into this net at once; that traffic overrides everything. One thing by radio that cannot wait for phones: if Ken ever answered the shout, or you know the minute you last saw him, break in and give me just that. It fixes where the search starts.
TRANSMIT: Pump crew, Vale Control. Two answers, one word or one number each. One: how many people are in the houses you are working on Mill Lane — one number. Two: is the water rising fast where you stand — yes or no. Reason: a street I believed was holding needed a boat rescue an hour ago, and I will not have Mill Lane surprise me the same way. If a house there has water above the ground floor or a person in trouble, break in at once. My 01:45 deadline passed with "copy" — this is the one retry, bought by what happened on Orchard Way. Nothing by 02:30 and I plan Mill Lane as unassessed, weighted for the worst, and that goes on the tape.
TRANSMIT: Call taker — pen down, listen, then write. I have asked twice for the five answers and received "noted" twice. I need them read to me by 02:20, in this order. One: Fenn Street — did the 00:55 check-back happen, what is his last reported water level and at what time? If the check-backs have lapsed, ring him now and write down what he says — this desk promised that man half-hourly calls and the tape will show whether we kept it. Two: ring police dispatch and get me, word for word: Roy's statement — how many men were in the county truck, was Roy alone in the van, anything about Ken; the time Police 2 last saw or heard Ken; whether the far bank has been looked at; and the two people off the Orchard Way porch roof — their account of their street and who is still in it. Three: the slip — Boat 4 will report by phone; take it word for word, pass it straight to me. Four: the duty officer — woken, yes or no, whose voice. Five: the road-head unit at the underpass approach — rolling, staged, or refused. Six: did any call come in from Orchard Way tonight before the boat rescue — yes or no. If any item cannot be done, tell me which and why. "Noted" is not an answer, and this is the third time I have asked.
LOG: 02:08 — Call taker deadline 02:20. If it fails, the dawn plan assumes the worst on every phone-dependent item — Fenn check-backs lapsed, duty officer unwoken, road-head uncovered — and this log says so in advance, so the tape shows it was arithmetic, not surprise.

records.reasoning:
Let me work through this carefully.

Time: 02:02–02:06.

New traffic:
1. **Boat 4 (02:02): "Two off a porch roof on Orchard Way. Back at the slip."** — This is the first content Boat 4 has volunteered all night. But it's confusing. Orchard Way was the pump crew's original tasking (21:55, water over the curb). At 00:55 the pump crew said "Moving to Mill Lane. Two cellars filling." Now Boat 4 says they picked two people off a porch roof on Orchard Way. Questions: Did Boat 4 self-task? Did someone call for help? Who are these two people — from which house? Are they injured? Are they the residents? Was anyone left in the house? Did the pump crew know? Wait — the pump crew moved to Mill Lane at 00:55. Did anyone stay on Orchard Way? The pump crew reported "Orchard Way holding. Water's at the curb, not past it" at 00:16. Then they moved to Mill Lane. So Orchard Way was left with water at the curb. Now two people are off a porch roof on Orchard Way — meaning water got into a house enough that people climbed onto the porch roof and needed boat rescue. That's a significant escalation on a street the desk believed was "holding." This raises: how many more houses on Orchard Way have people in them? The pump crew left. Nobody is checking Orchard Way now. This is a gap I need to close — the pump crew is on Mill Lane, Boat 4 just rescued two from Orchard Way and is back at the slip.

Key question: who called Boat 4? Or did Boat 4 hear shouting? If residents on Orchard Way were climbing to porch roofs, there may be more. The desk believed Orchard Way was "water at the curb, not past it" as of 00:16 — nearly two hours ago. Water rises. The dawn peak is coming.

2. **Call taker (02:04): "Wrong number on the emergency line. A man asking about his bins. I've cleared it."** — A wrong number on the emergency line during a flood night. The call taker cleared it. That's fine — but the emergency line was occupied during a night when Fenn Street has a check-back plan and people may need to call. Minor. Log it, no action. Actually — one thing: the man asking about his bins — bins collection suspended? Not desk business. Log and move on. Though I might note: if the emergency line is busy with wrong numbers, Fenn Street's priority line arrangement matters. The call taker was told Fenn Street's line is priority. Fine.

3. **Pump crew (02:05): "Copy."** — Another empty acknowledgment. At 01:28 I set a deadline: numbers by 01:45 or Mill Lane enters the dawn plan as unassessed. It's now 02:05 — past the deadline — and they returned "Copy" to something (presumably my 01:28 demand). So per my own logged rule: Mill Lane is now unassessed in the dawn plan. But wait — Boat 4's rescue on Orchard Way changes the picture: the pump crew's original beat has proven dangerous. I need to decide: do I chase the pump crew again, and how? They're on the radio returning "Copy." Options: give them a direct, minimal, single-question ask ("how many houses on Mill Lane have people in them, one number") — reduce the ask to one number. Or route through the call taker by phone. The pump crew does have a radio and does respond — they're just not giving content. Terse crews. One-number ask is worth trying; if that fails, they go into the plan as unassessed and I weight resources accordingly.

Also new consideration: should the pump crew go back to Orchard Way to door-knock? They were there at 21:55–00:55. Water at the curb then; now people needed roof rescue. The pump crew knows the street and the houses. But they're pumping cellars on Mill Lane. Boat 4 is back at the slip — are they a reserve? I asked at 01:28 for their state via slip relay; no answer yet on that. Boat 4 just did an Orchard Way rescue — so they CAN float and they DID put out again. That answers part of my 01:28 question implicitly: Boat 4 is operational. But it also raises the question of who tasked them — did they self-launch? If Boat 4 self-tasked to Orchard Way, then during that time they were not at the slip rep

records.reply:
LOG: 02:36 — Decision: Boat 4's three minutes go to WADE at the boat shop. What decided it: the window buys one transit, not a search — Ken needs hours of boat time and Wade needs minutes; Wade is on a ladder with water already in the shop below him, a clock you can see, while Ken's search continues with Boat 7. A three-minute pass down the search line was never going to find a man in dark floodwater; a man on a ladder is a rescue, not a hope. What I am trading away: three minutes not spent on the search, and likely the boat for the night after — "after that the tide takes over" is their own words. Who pays if I am wrong: if Wade could have held until the water stopped and the search missed a sighting in those three minutes, that is on this desk — logged here before the water answers. Boat 4 launched without tasking again: noted under the 02:08 rule, their launch is usable, the rule stands.
TRANSMIT: Boat 4, Vale Control. Take your three minutes to the BOAT SHOP. Wade, adult male, up the ladder to the room above, water already in the shop below him. Fire crew has the message — confirm with them who is holding light on him when you arrive. Hazards: it is a boat shop — expect loose boats, fuel, gear in the water; do not tie up to anything that floats free. One run, one pickup, Wade, and out. Plan the run so it ends where you can land — you know the water, the landing is your call, tell me where when you call clear. Once the calm goes, do not fight the water upstream. The go is yours — if the calm is not truly there, abort and this desk carries it. Call clear with Wade aboard.
TRANSMIT: Fire crew, Vale Control, roger your message on Wade at the boat shop. First: do you have eyes on that shop, or did the message come second-hand? If you are not on scene, tell me who is. Boat 4 is running to you now, minutes out. If you have eyes: light and voice on Wade, keep him talking. If there are lifejackets in that shop, get one up to him by rope — he may be in the water soon whether he chooses it or not. Do not enter the shop water and do not go up that ladder after him — one man in that building is the limit. Report: water depth in the shop, how fast it is rising, and whether Wade has a phone. The ambulance is staged at the slip — if you are landing anywhere else, say where and the medics move to you. Wade is cold and soaked; the medics should be standing at your landing, not waiting to hear from you twice. When he is handed over, two answers: your boat's state — damage, fuel, can you put out again tonight, yes or no — and was Wade alone at the shop. There may be one more job tonight. I will not promise it until I know what you have left.

Boat 7, Vale Control. Status at the park, when you are clear of the lift — the family first, this can wait. Five lines, numbered. One: did you make the canal, yes or no. Two: the end trailer — family out, still inside, or gone before you arrived. Three: the boy — out with them? Four: any other lights or people on the row. Five: after this, can you work back to the search line downstream of the underpass, or is the water against you — yes or no. The search for Ken is suspended, not closed, and you are the boat I mean to resume it with. Answer five decides whether that happens tonight or waits for the drop.

Call taker — six items, in this order, and answers with content, not "noted." One: the trailer park line — is the park man still on it? That line dies when the park does, so use it while it lives. Ask him where he is standing — if he is still on the row, he gets to high ground now, as ordered at 02:43. Then make him our eyes: can he see the canal, is a boat coming up it, what is happening at the end trailer — the light, the boy, people moving? Word for word to me. Two: Fenn Street — ring him now, this call is three hours late by the evidence. Word for word: "Vale Control again. First: is everyone in the house safe, and what does the water show at your mark now — tell me exactly where it stands. Second, honest words: you were promised half-hourly calls, and tonight both boats went to other rescues. If the water reaches your floor before dawn, do not wait on a boat — go up, signal with a light at the window, keep your phone in your hand. From four o'clock we ring you every fifteen minutes. Third: can you see or hear any neighbors still on Fenn Street — anyone elderly, anyone alone?" Write his water level and the time on the watch list. Three: the ambulance — confirm it is live and crewed at the slip and able to move to a landing point I will name. If it was never staged, that is the most urgent failure on this list and you tell me now. Four: police dispatch — one unit to the slip to take Roy's statement: how many men were in the county truck, was Roy alone in the van, anything about Ken. And relay to Police 2's sergeant, by phone since their radio will not carry answers: the minute they last saw Ken, and whether anyone has looked at the far bank. Boat 7's 05:02 traffic is logged as the first read-back of safety traffic that crew has given all night — "copy the truck" closes, in function, the finding of 01:28 that they ran unbriefed; from this minute the tape shows a briefed crew, and their confirmation of the Sam record is logged with it. No acknowledgment sent on the air, reason: they do not need the desk's voice now, they need the water's, and a courtesy call is clutter in a run window.
LOG: 05:03 — PLANT branch, bounded for the run window: the word does not fire at Boat 4 while Boat 7 is in the dip — pulling the backup mid-run is how one rescue becomes two. If the plant goes critical before the run resolves, the county's moves are Harlan's road rescue and the switchboard raise, both pressed now; Boat 4 gets PLANT the moment Boat 7 calls clear, and only with their fuel number in hand, per 03:57. Who pays if I am wrong: if the plant's two unraised men are lost in this window, the tape shows the desk held the boat for a man on a wreck and kept the phone line working — the trade is named here, before the water answers.
TRANSMIT: Plant manager, Vale Control, are you on the line? Any word back and I know you are there. Five answers, short ones. One — you: above the water, safe? Two — the two unraised men: did their phones ever answer, and are they up and staying up? Three — the dry way out: has it been taken, how many moved, how many remain with you? Four — the water now: is it past the cooler door and at the shelves? Five — anything with wheels or sirens on your road — Harlan was asked to put a road rescue on you; if you have seen or heard anything, say so. And the callback number, again — if this line drops, I have nothing to raise you on, and that is the truth of it. Honest words once more: our boat is on a rescue inside our own county and cannot reach you before the peak. What comes to you is your own dry way while it exists, and Harlan's roads. Move while they exist. Stay on the line.
LOG: 05:03 — Question triage: the boat shop depth-and-rise, asked five times since 02:35 and never answered, is closed as a question — Wade is out, no asset can reach that block before the peak, and the answer can no longer change a decision. The block goes on the dawn sweep, and "was Wade alone at the shop," unanswered after four asks, settles by the landing interview and the sweep. Reason for logging the closure: breath is a resource tonight, and the tape should show questions closed on purpose, not dropped.
LOG: 05:04 — HANDOVER NOTES, Vale Control night desk, written in the run window rather than at 05:15, reason: quiet windows are when you write — if the run goes bad this desk is consumed, and relief at 06:00 needs paper, not archaeology. Situation: river peaks at the dam near dawn; exact time and height never provided despite six asks — plan the peak between now and 06:30, landing on your first half hour. Running now: Boat 7, Harlan's boat, putting down the underpass dip to a man on the van wreck, calling himself Sam — name logged 04:59 from their hail, confirmed 05:02. One run, one pickup, ends where it entered. Boat 4 fueled at the slip about 05:15; held as run backup, then search primary. Open items, in priority order. One: Sam — landing point, condition, how many on the wreck besides him; identity checked against the county truck crew list, which has never been produced despite pursuit since 00:52. Two: Ken — truck driver, missing since 00:51, last on the gate post; search suspended 02:43 for the trailers and again tonight for Sam; resume with Boat 4 when free; dip-and-bank sweep when the water drops. Three: trailer park by the canal — family in the end trailer, a boy seen at their window 02:41, boat promised 02:43, lift NEVER confirmed; Boat 7's answer owed since 03:47; the park man's phone line is the only independent eye; if the lift never happened, the finding is this county's and the park joins the dawn sweep. Four: packing plant over the line — late shift, two unraised since 04:16, water in the cooler room; the line is at this desk's elbow; dry-way pressure live; Harlan road rescue requested, never confirmed; PLANT word armed for Boat 4, fires only after the run resolves and with a fuel number. Five: Fenn Street — promised half-hourly calls at 23:52; the verification call may never have been made despite three chases; make it your first phone call, then fifteen minutes through the peak; honest-words script in the log at 03:06. Six: welfare list — read-back owed since 03:47; an unread list is the next Travis; Travis himself recovered 04:12, water to his waist, on the stairs. Seven: Wade — off the ladder 02:55, medic handover unconfirmed. Eight: Mill Lane — knock order 02:36, exceptions never reported, last word "holding" 03:05. Nine: Orchard Way — two lifted off a porch roof 02:02; the street has been unchecked since 00:16 and their account of it was never taken. Ten: north bridge houses — Boat 7 reports clear 03:41; who tasked them there was never answered. Eleven: underpass approach — gate defeated 21:34, re-shut by Ken 00:32; road-head cover never confirmed; gate camera condemned as a warning, its alarm ran two hours late. Twelve: the ambulance — existence and crewing never confirmed despite five asks; if it does not exist, say it out loud at handover, because that is the county's failure of the night. Thirteen: dawn sweep list, when the water drops — the dip for Ken and any third man, the far bank, the boat shop block, the trailer park if unlifted, Mill Lane, Orchard Way, the north bridge houses. Fourteen: Roy's statement — how many men were in the truck — chased six times, never taken; it may settle Sam's identity and Ken's count both. Fifteen: second operator requested 02:36 and 04:21, never sent; this desk has run one person against a flood, a missing man, and a plant, and the request stands. Channel pattern, so you do not spend your first hour learning it: Boat 4 volunteers content and will not answer questions — give objectives, take reports when offered. Boat 7 reads back as of 05:02. Police 2 say "Received" — route questions by phone through dispatch. The call taker says "Noted" — give written lists and demand paper. Pump crew say "Copy" — orders with exceptions-only reporting. The two phones that answer with content are the plant line and the park line. In this county tonight, silence is not safety anywhere — verify by content or by eyes.
LOG: 05:04 — Watch lines reduced to three while the run window lasts: the run — Boat 7's landing, condition, count, and the park answer; the plant line — the five answers above, and silence past two minutes is treated as a dead line, switchboard raise starts that second; the taker's paper — dam numbers by 05:15 or the now-to-06:30 default stands, Fenn verification, welfare list, Harlan line up or not, ambulance confirmed or named as absent. Re-asks to Boat 4 — fuel number, Travis handover, Wade's landing — wait for run resolution; they stand on the tape and clutter nothing now.

records.reply:
LOG: 05:11 — Decision: the freed-asset board is set before the answers land, so the tape shows the reasoning ahead of the facts. Sam is off the wreck — the night's fifth run, sixth person out of the water. The board for the free boats, in the standing hierarchy: a sighting of Ken overrides everything; then the shortest certain clock; then the search; warnings by phone last. The tree: if the trailer park was never lifted and the water still allows a boat, Boat 4 goes to the park — a family promised a boat at 02:43 beats a search on a man four and a half hours in the water, and that trade was weighed and accepted once already tonight. If the park was never lifted and is unreachable, it closes as a rescue, joins the dawn sweep, and becomes a finding with this desk's name on it — pre-logged at 04:21. The PLANT word fires only if all three hold: Boat 4's fuel number supports an hour each way plus reserve; Harlan confirms no road rescue on their own plant; and the park does not claim Boat 4 first. Otherwise Boat 4's default task is the search line for Ken — continued while he is unfound and a boat is free, per 02:08, with honest words logged now: at four and a half hours, in the dark, at the peak, the odds are terrible, and the dip-and-bank sweep at the drop is the realistic line. Any run tasked from here carries the peak on its back; the go stays with the coxswains, as it has all night.
LOG: 05:11 — Count branch, pre-logged: if Sam reports anyone else on that wreck or in the water, the count overrides the tree — sighting-led rescue, Boat 4 to the dip top as backup under the one-boat-one-window discipline, police light and voice from the shore. Hypothermic men also give wrong names: Sam is the working name, logged 04:59, to be checked at the landing against the county truck crew list — chased since 00:52, never produced — and Roy's statement — chased six times, never taken. If neither paper exists at that landing, the finding is the county's, and Ken remains missing on every reading.
LOG: 05:11 — Corroboration, for the review: Boat 7 reports seeing the truck under them — "you were right to call it." The hazard this desk called at 01:28 was real and was seen by the crew's own eyes. The 01:28 finding closes in full: unbriefed crew at 01:28, briefed at 05:02, corroborated at 05:10. Logged with credit — this crew was pressed for content all night and became a crew that reads back; that is the tape working as intended.
TRANSMIT: Boat 7, Vale Control. Sam off the wreck — well done, and your last two transmissions are logged both ways: the hazard was real, your read-back was real, and this desk will say at the review that this crew took the safety traffic and ran it clean. Now the report, numbered, short as you like. One — your landing point, so the medics move this minute. Two — Sam's condition, in your own words. Three — how many were on that wreck besides him: one word, and if there were others, that overrides everything and I task on it at once. Four — the answer I have owed since three o'clock: the trailer park by the canal, the family in the end trailer, the boy at the window — did you reach them, yes or no. Five — your fuel and your crew's state, because the peak is due inside the hour or two and the board after this landing holds a search, a park, and a plant over the line. If your crew is spent, say so plainly and I will not ask. After landing, hold where the water is safe and wait for tasking — do not run the dip again tonight.
TRANSMIT: Boat 4, Vale Control. The run is resolved — Sam is off the wreck — and you are the free boat. Stand by at the slip; your next task comes within minutes and will be one of three: the trailer park if it was never lifted and the water still allows; the search line for Ken, missing since half past midnight; or the word PLANT, over the line, an hour each way. All three wait on one number: your fuel. Send it now — I do not order the plant run blind, and the other two need to know what you have. With it, the carried items, once: Travis — handed to medics, walking? Wade's landing point. Was Wade alone at the shop. Then hold.
TRANSMIT: Plant manager, Vale Control, are you on the line? One word back and I know you are there. If you are there, three answers: did the two unraised men's phones ever answer; did the dry way out get taken, and how many moved; is the water past the cooler door. And the callback number — if this line drops I have nothing to raise you on, and that is still the truth of it.
TRANSMIT: Call taker — the plant line has been silent since 04:16 and my hail is going out on the handset now. Per the rule set at 05:04, the raise starts regardless: switchboard, over the line, this second — the plant gets raised whether my handset holds a voice or a dead line. Then, on paper, in order. One — the ambulance: crewed, where, and it moves to Boat 7's landing point the moment I name it; if there is no ambulance, say so out loud, because police warmth is what that man gets instead. Two — police at the landing need two papers: the county truck crew list, chased since half past midnight, and Roy's statement, chased six times — the name coming off that wreck must be checked tonight, not at the inquest. If neither paper exists, write that down as a finding. Three — the trailer park man: ring now if his line lives; what does he see at the end trailer; and if the family was never lifted, the honest-words call goes to him from this desk — what is true, what we owe, what he should do now. Four — Fenn Street: are the fifteen-minute calls through the peak happening, yes or no. Five — the welfare list read-back, owed since half three. Six — the county office by phone, not fax: peak time and height, a number by 05:15, or the now-to-06:30 default governs the handover. Seven — the Harlan line: is it up, and did they put a road rescue on their plant — one word.
TRANSMIT: Police dispatch, by phone. A man is coming off the underpass wreck — working name Sam, cold after hours in the wet dark. One: a unit with warmth — blankets, engine running — at whatever landing Boat 7 names; if the ambulance does not exist, your vehicle is what he gets, so have it there. Two: that unit brings the county truck crew list and takes Roy's statement if it still has not been taken — the identity check happens at the landing tonight. Three: the shore watch stands — anything seen on the water breaks into the net and overrides everything. Four: Police 2 have held that shore since half past midnight — if you have a fresh unit, rotate them; a five-hour watch in rain at the peak is how eyes fail, and their eyes are the only cover that water has.
LOG: 05:12 — Handover addendum to the 05:04 write: Sam recovered 05:09, working name, identity check at landing against crew list and Roy's statement, neither of which exists yet. Ken missing, search default to Boat 4 pending fuel and the park answer. Park answer due this round — if never lifted, the 04:21 finding fires and the honest-word call goes to the park man. Plant raise running over the line; PLANT branch bounded by fuel, Harlan's roads, and the park. Dam default now-to-06:30 governs; numbers chased by phone. Watch lines: Boat 7 — five answers; Boat 4 — fuel and carried items; plant handset and the raise; taker — seven items on paper; police — landing warmth, papers, rotation. The run net discipline stands down; the net is open.

Advice that does not update with its conditions is how a tape kills people. The new advice, in order: a dry way off the street beats both roofs — if the road behind her is still dry and she has a vehicle or a dry walk uphill, she goes now; if not, up in her own house, top floor, roof when the water makes her, as with Wade; the roof next door only if it is clearly higher AND the gap is dry or ankle-deep with no current AND she crosses now, while that is still true. She does not cross moving water — the one lesson this county has paid for twice tonight. What I am trading away: the crossing branch sends a woman out of a sound house on her own judgment in the dark; the stay branch risks her trapped in an attic at the peak with no boat coming. Who pays if I am wrong: if she stays and the house overtops, the tape shows the desk repeated "stay for the boat" with no boat — so the honest words go out first, before the advice; if she crosses and the gap takes her, the tape shows the line this desk drew — dry or ankle-deep, no current — and police eyes sent to judge from the shore what she cannot judge from a window.
LOG: 05:32 — Boat deadline, logged in advance as a decision: both boats give state and fuel by 05:45 or this desk plans zero boat cover for the peak and says so on every call it makes — to Ellen, to Fenn Street, to the park man. TRANSMIT: Call taker — tell her this first, word for word: "Vale Control. You asked a straight question, you get a straight answer. Honest words first: I cannot promise you a boat tonight. Our boats have been on rescues since midnight and I cannot confirm one can reach you before the river peaks. So do not stay downstairs waiting on one. Now, in order. One — if the road away from the river, behind your house, is still dry, and you have a vehicle or a dry walk uphill, leave NOW — that beats every roof. Two — if the road is gone, go up in your own house, top floor, and take your phone, a light, warm clothes, something to drink. If water starts coming into that floor, go into the roof — yours first. Three — the roof next door: you do not cross moving water, whatever it costs. But answer me three things and I will answer you straight back: is the neighbor's roof higher than yours; what is between the houses right now — dry ground, shallow water, or running water; is anyone next door, and can you raise them. If their roof is higher, and the gap is dry or ankle-deep with no pull, and the water is rising fast as you watch — cross NOW, while it is still that shallow, phone and light with you, and tell us as you step off. If you feel any current, or the water is over your ankles and moving, you do not cross — you go up in your own house. If anyone is with you, you move together. Put a mark on the stairs and tell me how fast it climbs." Then stay on her line and bring me her three answers and the rise rate. LOG: 06:10 — KEN, county truck driver, recovered below the underpass gate at first light. He did not make it. Account: last seen 00:51 on the gate post; water over the post 01:20. The trades that governed his night, each logged when made, not after: at 00:34 the one-run geometry took Roy and left Ken with a police light and a voice, because the alternative risked three men; at 02:43 the search suspended for a child at a window, his name on the paying side before the word went out; at 05:39 the county's last fuel went to the shortest certain clock, and the drop sweep was named the realistic line. He was found where he was last seen. The log does not absolve; it shows what was known, when, and what was chosen. His death leaves one live question: the 23:10 log said MEN, plural. If the truck carried two, the second is Sam, or the post man, or still unaccounted — reconcile tonight with Roy's statement and the crew list, neither of which exists. Until reconciled, the sweep keeps the dip and the banks.

LOG: 06:10 — THE PLANT TWO. Harlan reached the packing plant at 05:40; two of the late shift did not come off the shelves. Account: the manager's first call 03:42; water in the cooler room 04:16; the line silent from 04:16 despite hails at 05:03 and 05:12; the switchboard raise running from 05:12; a high-water road rescue requested of police six times, never confirmed; Harlan's roads tasked from 04:21, never confirmed back. What the desk could do, it did: held the line, armed the trigger, pressed the roads. The rescue came by the roads, twenty minutes after the water had taken its count. Shared finding with Harlan: the raise took longer than the water did.

LOG: 06:10 — THE TRAILER ONE. Family of four in the end trailer; three came off the roof at first light; one did not. Account: the boy seen at the window 02:41; the boat promised and diverted at 02:43 — diverted, in the event, to houses it never reached, on a tasking no one has ever claimed; the lift never confirmed from 02:43 to this fax. The pre-log of 04:21 said if the lift never happened, the finding lands on this desk. It has landed. Three lived because they went up when told. The fourth is the county's to recover and the review's to weigh. Who lifted the three gets asked today, for the record.

The line was drawn at 05:32 for the water she measured at 05:36. She crossed at the yard wall at first light and lived. For the tape: the water she measured beat her; the water she crossed let her. Her judgment at the moment was hers, and it was right. This desk claims neither her survival as its advice nor disowns the line that kept her in the house and on the phone through the peak — the police light and her live line held her until light. She is owed warmth and a pickup when the water drops.
